citation: Rathfelder et al., Process optimization to produce anisotropic NdFeB permanent magnets from recycled powder via powder extrusion
feedstock_family: End-of-life NdFeB powder processed by HPMS
route: Powder extrusion moulding with in-situ magnetic particle alignment followed by sintering

reported_results.oxygen_change: Approximately 0.4 wt% increase from HPMS powder to sintered part; source-specific

limitations: Br/Js is an alignment ratio and is not absolute remanence Br.
Reported values are specific to the study's feedstock, process, specimen and methods.
Does not qualify MEX, LPBF, SmCo, SmFeN, ferrite, unrelated recovered lots or production-scale process capability.

citation: State-of-the-art additive manufacturing of NdFeB permanent magnets: challenges and pathways toward high performance
journal: Journal of Science: Advanced Materials and Devices
reported_findings: The surveyed MEX route has the highest remanence among the printed NdFeB routes reviewed.
LPBF can produce dense material but magnetic texture remains a limiting issue.
The review identifies retention of Nd2Fe14B phase and magnetic texture as important high-performance challenges.
limitations: Aggregated studies are not a matched process comparison.
No universal route ranking or production-performance value is implied.
